audit.why: Rated EVEN at 47.55% over 1186 games. Mel's W reflects Brand's Q/W/R, so the lane mechanics favor her even while the aggregate WR sits under 50 — Brand's teamfight R and Blaze spread do the WR damage outside lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart is blanket 'Skill'; content win[] and packet chart both say Mel everywhere except Brand at level 6. Full phases[4].why also describes Mel winning a row the chart gives Brand.
audit.why: Content and packet agree; Brand's only clean window is Pyroclasm plus triple-Blaze detonation at 6, and post-first-item Rebuttal reclaims the poke war.
audit.corrected: Sides set Mel/Brand per win[], phases[4].why rewritten to a Brand-favored explanation.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text claims 'every ability he throws is a targetable projectile you can punish' — false: Conflagration (E) is a point-and-click blast, not a projectile, and Rebuttal does not answer it. breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; two Do's/Don'ts bullets were tradeGood/tradeBad pasted verbatim.
audit.why: Brand Q 8s rank 1 (stun only on ablaze targets), W 10s-8s, E 13s-9s point-and-click, R 100s. Q, W and R are projectile/reflectable; E is not.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — the execute threshold turns your chip war into a countdown he can see.
edits.after: Pyroclasm bounces plus a triple-Blaze detonation is his one burst window — don't eat a stun at 6.

edits.before: - Brand Sear (Stun): matchup-defining — Q only stuns when you are ablaze — after eating W or E, the stun line is the dodge that matters. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Rebuttal like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Brand Sear (Q): 8s at rank 1 — it only stuns while you're ablaze; after eating W or E, that line is the dodge that matters. - Pillar of Flame (W): 10s down to 8 — his poke lives here; step up in the gap. - Pyroclasm: 100s. Rebuttal reflects Q, W and R — never E.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Solar Snare roots at 1000 range, past his 625-range E — root the walk-up and the full volley lands on a Brand who cannot answer.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: The 11-second root is your kill setup, not a spacing tool — an E spent shooing him off a minion leaves the real window with no lock.

edits.before: After Level 6 the lane swings back to you. W Rebuttal is enormous here — reflect his W or R bounce back at him and you win the poke war outright, since every ability he throws is a targetable projectile you can punish.
edits.after: After Level 6 the lane swings back to you. W Rebuttal is enormous here — reflect his Q, W or R bounce back at him and you win the poke war outright. Only Conflagration (E) is point-and-click and slips past the reflect.

notes: Packet flags the level chart contradicting the 47.55% WR (Mel 6/7 stages). The chart is kit-grounded — Rebuttal reflects three of Brand's four damage spells — so the WR gap likely comes from teamfights, not lane stages; left the chart shape, flagged here. Full sides edited alone since content win[] already held the correct values (no win[N] no-ops). Corrected the false 'every ability is a projectile' claim: Conflagration (E) is point-and-click, unreflectable.
